sentences.t: This laptop cost me a hundred and forty-nine dollars, and I genuinely did not expect it to turn on.
Today we find out if it's a bargain or just e-waste with a keyboard.

Okay, unboxing.
The box is about as thin as a pizza box and weighs roughly the same.
Inside, laptop, a charger with a very long cable, and a manual that's mostly in German for some reason.
Out of the box it actually looks fine, it's a silver plastic shell trying very hard to look like aluminum.
If you squint from across the room, you might think it's something nicer.
Up close, the lid flexes when you open it, which is not ideal.
Specs, it's got an Intel Celeron, four gigs of RAM, and sixty-four gigabytes of storage, which is less than my phone.
The screen is fourteen inches and, let's be generous, it's a screen.
Let's turn it on.
Okay, it's thinking.
Still thinking.
And we're in Windows setup after about a minute, which is honestly better than I feared.
Setup took a little over twenty minutes, and then it immediately wanted to install updates.
And here's the first real problem, the updates need more space than the laptop has free.
Out of sixty-four gigs, Windows was already using about forty, so I had to plug in a USB stick just to update it.
Alright, real-world use.
I opened a browser with three tabs, email, a document, and YouTube, and it was usable, sluggish, but usable.
Opening a fourth tab with a news site full of ads and it just froze for about eight seconds.
YouTube at 1080p stuttered, at 720p it was smooth, so lower your expectations a bit.
Typing on it is actually not bad, the keys are mushy but they're spaced fine.
The trackpad, on the other hand, I would describe as a suggestion.
Battery life, I got about five and a half hours of light browsing, which surprised me.
The speakers, though, sound like someone talking inside a cereal box, so bring headphones.
And the webcam is technically a webcam, but on a video call my friend asked if I was calling from a submarine.
So, the verdict.
If you need something for a kid to do homework on, or a backup machine for email and documents, it kind of works.
If you want to do anything more than that, save up another hundred bucks and buy a used business laptop instead, you'll get way more for your money.
Let me know what cheap tech you want me to suffer through next.
